title: Goldman's Boss Calls 5% Normal. History Agrees
transcript: Around 5% that's the interest rate on a 10-year US government bond right now. That sounds high. Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon says it doesn't worry him. >> And for most of my life, except for the last 15 years, the 10-year Treasury has been higher than 5%. >> He's right. [music] In his lifetime, the 10-year has closed above 5% on more than half of all trading days. In 1981 it hit almost 16%. [music] Then came the financial crisis and money got cheap. In 2020 it fell to about [music] half a percent. And the cheap stretch ran even longer. No close above 5% from July 2007 until this September. 19 years. A whole generation of investors never saw it. [music] So 5% is not strange. The last two decades were >> And we can have a very very vibrant economy with that, but it's a different it's a different operating environment. >> Cheap money was the exception. 5% is the old normal.

key_warnings: The 10-year US Treasury yield at 5% represents a return to historical norms after an exceptional 19-year period of artificially suppressed interest rates (2007-2026). This shift signals a structural change in the operating environment for investors and the broader economy. A generation of investors have operated exclusively in a cheap money regime and must adapt to fundamentally different market conditions and valuation frameworks.
